display.purpose: Hero headline, section headings, card titles.

label.purpose: Domain tags, milestone chips, grade labels, footer line.

motion.name: rise-in
motion.purpose: One-time staggered entrance for route waypoints on initial paint. Additive only — never gates visibility, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single call-to-action treatment. Mono uppercase label, tracked.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; background: #a94a18; color: #f2e9d6; padding: 12px 24px; border-radius: 2px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; transition: background 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #7e3712; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #f0b98a; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Goal Chip
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-block; background: #ffffff; color: #5a5140; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 9999px; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #d8c9a8; font-size: 0.8125rem; }

components.name: Waypoint Marker
components.description: Signature component: a numbered, difficulty-graded route marker with a stamped-metal inset.
components.css: .ds-waypoint { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 40px; height: 40px; border-radius: 9999px; color: #f2e9d6; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; box-shadow: inset 0 2px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.35), inset 0 -1px 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.15); } .ds-waypoint--beginner { background: #3e5c2c; } .ds-waypoint--intermediate { background: #3e6e82; } .ds-waypoint--advanced { background: #2a241c; }

components.name: Signpost Panel
components.description: The one lifted surface in the system — the hero's goal-input action panel.
components.css: .ds-signpost { background: #f2e9d6; color: #201b12; padding: 24px; border-radius: 2px; box-shadow: 0 18px 40px -16px rgba(0,0,0,0.55); } .ds-signpost__label { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.6875rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.14em; color: #5a5140; }

narrative.overview: PathFinder's visual world is a national-park trailhead at dusk: a routed wood sign at the edge of the woods, graded difficulty blazes marking the route ahead, a topographic contour map fading into the tree line. The product's core mechanism — turning a stated goal into a sequenced, prerequisite-aware route — is literally a marked trail, not a course-catalog grid. The category default this world refuses: gradient-hero EdTech SaaS with duotone feature cards and a stock photo of laughing laptop users. The system is quiet and unadorned. It commits to a real material world (routed signage, painted blazes, engraved markers) through restrained, intentional gestures — a lifted signpost panel, a stamped-metal inset on numbered waypoint markers — rather than literal wood-grain texture or skeuomorphic decoration, which would read as costume rather than craft.
keyCharacteristics: Deep forest-charcoal ground as the dominant field, warm parchment-cream as the carried 'signage' surface
A single confident rust-orange accent, used only for the primary action and active blaze markers
Difficulty grading expressed as real trail-blaze colors, reused as a functional system, not decoration
Zilla Slab display type with carved-sign character, paired with Archivo's wayfinding-grotesk body text
Flat by default; depth appears only where the world's own materials would have it

rules.name: The One Blaze Rule
rules.body: Rust-orange is the only saturated accent on any given screen. It appears exactly where the visitor can act or where a route is actively marked. It never decorates.

rules.name: The Graded-Not-Generic Rule
rules.body: Difficulty is always shown through the three named blaze colors, never through generic success/warning/danger status colors.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No small label ever sits directly above a heading as a kicker.

rules.name: The Two-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Only the signpost lift and the stamped disc exist as shadows anywhere in the system.

dos: Do keep rust-orange to one saturated use per screen.
Do express difficulty/level through the three named blaze colors everywhere in the product.
Do let headings carry their own weight — no eyebrow/kicker labels.
Do darken (not brighten) interactive colors on hover.
Do reuse the waypoint-marker language for any future sequence, timeline, or progress UI.
donts: Don't introduce a second saturated accent color.
Don't add literal wood-grain, paper-fiber, or metal-brush texture images.
Don't use generic status colors — the palette's trio means difficulty grade, not status.
Don't add a card-grid feature-list section — the system's structure is sequence-first.
